intro: In these questions the signs of an equation are hidden, coded or mixed up. You choose the signs (or the swap) that make the equation true. Everything depends on doing × and ÷ before + and −.

tips.title: × and ÷ before + and −
tips.body: Work out × and ÷ first, from left to right. Then do + and −, from left to right. In 12 + 12 − 12 ÷ 12 − 12, first 12 ÷ 12 = 1, which leaves 12 + 12 − 1 − 12 = 11.
tips.caption: × and ÷ first, then + and −.

tips.title: Brackets come first of all
tips.body: Anything inside ( ), { } or [ ] is worked out before the rest. (5 + 2) × 15 ÷ 105 = 7 × 15 ÷ 105 = 105 ÷ 105 = 1.

tips.title: Try the options one by one
tips.body: Put each option's signs into the * places in order and work the equation out. Look at the answer's size first: much bigger than the numbers means a × is needed; much smaller means ÷ or −. That rules out some options straight away.

tips.title: Letters or shapes for signs
tips.body: When K means +, L means × and so on, first write the equation again with the real signs, and only then work it out. 50 K 40 L 30 M 20 N 10 becomes 50 + 40 × 30 ÷ 20 − 10 = 50 + 60 − 10 = 100.

tips.title: Signs with changed meanings
tips.body: If "+ means ÷", every + in an option is really a ÷. Rewrite the whole option before working it out: {(19 × 11) + 15} ÷ 2 becomes {(19 + 11) ÷ 15} − 2 = 2 − 2 = 0.

tips.title: Swapping two signs or two numbers
tips.body: Swap the two signs (or numbers) in the equation, work out the left side and compare it with the right side. In 12 + 3 × 5 ÷ 5 − 1 = 36, swap × and +: 12 × 3 + 5 ÷ 5 − 1 = 36 + 1 − 1 = 36.
